claim: A degron::3xFLAG tag was introduced into the 3' end of the daf-2 open reading frame using CRISPR.
source: To monitor and conditionally regulate protein levels of the C. elegans DAF-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor, we introduced a degron::3xFLAG tag into the 3' end of the daf-2 open reading frame (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the method used to tag the DAF-2 receptor and references a figure showing the construct.

claim: The degron::3xFLAG insertion was designed to tag the DAF-2 receptor at the cytosolic part to minimize interference with receptor function.
source: This degron::3xFLAG insertion into the genome was designed to tag the DAF-2 receptor at the cytosolic part for two reasons: first, to minimize any interference by the 81-amino acids large degron::3xFLAG-tag with the DAF-2 receptor function; and second, to ensure accessibility of the degron for targeted degradation by the TIR1 ubiquitin ligase expressed in the cytoplasm (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript provides explicit reasoning for the design choice and references Figure 1A showing the schematic.

claim: Western blot analysis detected a specific band in daf-2(bch40) animals that was absent in wild type (N2) and animals carrying only the TIR1 transgene.
source: We performed western blot analysis against the 3xFLAG-tag and detected a specific band in daf-2(bch40) animals. This band was absent in wild type (N2) and animals carrying only the eft-3p::TIR1::mRuby::unc-54 3'UTR transgene (Figure 1B), which expresses TIR1 in all somatic cells, including neurons (Tomioka et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental data from western blot analysis shown in Figure 1B, with citation to support TIR1 expression pattern.

claim: The band detected by western blot was confirmed to be DAF-2::degron::3xFLAG by treatment with daf-2 RNAi, which caused the band to nearly completely disappear after 48 hr.
source: To verify whether the band from the western blot was indeed DAF-2::degron::3xFLAG, we treated DAF-2::degron animals with daf-2 RNAi. The band nearly completely disappeared after 48 hr of daf-2(RNAi) feeding (Figure 1C and D, Source data 1 and Source data 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes an RNAi experiment with quantitative results shown in figures.

claim: The tagged transmembrane receptor DAF-2 did not interfere with normal DAF-2 function.
source: Collectively, these results suggested that the tagged transmembrane receptor DAF-2 did not interfere with normal DAF-2 function.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results showing normal development and function.

claim: Wild-type DAF-2::degron::3xFLAG levels were comparable across a range of temperatures (15–28°C).
source: We observed comparable wild-type DAF-2::degron::3xFLAG levels across a range of temperatures (15–28°C; Figure 1E), indicating that temperature does not influence DAF-2 levels in wild type.
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations from western blot analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Temperature does not influence DAF-2 levels in wild type.
source: We observed comparable wild-type DAF-2::degron::3xFLAG levels across a range of temperatures (15–28°C; Figure 1E), indicating that temperature does not influence DAF-2 levels in wild type.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temperature experiment data.

claim: DAF-2 protein almost completely disappeared after 36–48 hr of starvation.
source: Intriguingly, however, we found that using FLAG-HRP antibodies to monitor protein levels, DAF-2 protein almost completely disappeared after 36–48 hr of starvation (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental data from western blot analysis shown in Figures 1F and G.

claim: Well-fed animals with 1% glucose added to the bacterial diet increased DAF-2 protein levels.
source: In keeping with this result, well-fed animals, for which we added 1% glucose into the bacterial diet (OP50), increased the DAF-2 protein levels (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental data from western blot analysis shown in Figures 1F and G.

claim: Starvation-induced degradation of DAF-2 did not happen when animals were fed HT1115 bacterial strain during development.
source: Curiously, we noted that this starvation-induced degradation of DAF-2 did not happen when, during development, C. elegans were fed another bacterial strain, HT1115, used for RNAi (L4440). When DAF-2::degron animals were grown on L4440 and then shifted on empty NGM plates for 24 or 48 hr of starvation, DAF-2 levels did not decrease (Figure 1H).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations from western blot analysis shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The nutritional composition of the animal's diet prior to starvation influences DAF-2 stability.
source: This observation suggests a hypothesis that the nutritional composition of the animal's diet prior to starvation influences DAF-2 stability, which will be interesting to test in future research.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their observations.

claim: Food availability controls DAF-2 receptor abundance.
source: We conclude that food availability controls not only the secretion of insulin-like peptides to regulate DAF-2 activity (Pierce et al., 2001) but also DAF-2 receptor abundance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data, with citation to support the known role of food in insulin-like peptide secretion.

claim: After 30 min of 1 mM auxin treatment, there was a dramatic decrease in transmembrane DAF-2 protein abundance.
source: In keeping with that hypothesis, after 30 min of 1 mM auxin treatment, we observed a dramatic decrease in transmembrane DAF-2 protein abundance (Figure 1I and J).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental data from western blot analysis shown in Figures 1I and J.

claim: After 24 hr of 1 mM auxin treatment, there was only a 40% total decrease in DAF-2 protein abundance rather than a complete loss.
source: After 24 hr of 1 mM auxin treatment, we observed only a 40% total decrease in DAF-2 protein abundance rather than a complete loss (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative data from western blot analysis shown in Figures 1C and D.

claim: The AID system allows for the partial, rapid degradation of the transmembrane DAF-2 receptor.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that our AID system allows for the partial, rapid degradation of the transmembrane DAF-2 receptor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetics experiments showing DAF-2 degradation.

claim: Within 1 hr of 1 mM auxin treatment, most DAF-16::GFP translocated into the nuclei in DAF-2::degron animals.
source: Within 1 hr of 1 mM auxin treatment, we found that most DAF-16::GFP translocated into the nuclei in DAF-2::degron animals (Figure 2B), with observable translocation already after 30 min (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 2B and supplement.

claim: DAF-16::GFP nuclear localization in DAF-2::degron animals was time- and auxin-concentration-dependent.
source: This DAF-16::GFP nuclear localization in DAF-2::degron animals was time- and auxin-concentration-dependent and did not occur in DAF-16::GFP animals with wild-type DAF-2 (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations from fluorescence microscopy shown in figures.

claim: SKN-1- or DAF-16-target gene expression of gst-4 or sod-3 was only induced upon auxin treatment in DAF-2::degron animals.
source: Similarly, SKN-1- or DAF-16-target gene expression of gst-4 or sod-3 was only induced upon auxin treatment in DAF-2::degron animals (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental data from reporter assays shown in Figures 2C and D.

claim: IIS is reduced upon AID DAF-2 degradation.
source: Thus, expectedly, IIS is reduced upon AID DAF-2 degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the DAF-16 translocation and target gene expression data.

claim: Synchronized L1 treated with 0.1 or 1 mM auxin all formed dauers at 25°C.
source: However, synchronized L1 treated with 0.1 or 1 mM auxin all formed dauers at 25°C (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations shown in Figures 2E and F.

claim: Lower auxin concentrations (1, 10, and 50 μM) caused dose-dependent retardation of developmental speed, but the offspring of retarded animals grown on plates containing auxin became dauers.
source: We observed dose-dependent retardation of the developmental speed when using lower auxin concentrations (1, 10, and 50 μM), but the offspring of retarded animals, grown on plates containing auxin, became dauers (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations shown in Figures 2E and F.

claim: The dependence on auxin concentration for dauer formation of L1 animals suggests a threshold of DAF-2 receptor levels for the decision or commitment to dauer diapause.
source: The dependence on auxin concentration for dauer formation of L1 animals suggests a threshold of DAF-2 receptor levels for the decision or commitment to dauer diapause.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the dose-response data.

claim: Dauer formation was observed at 15°C and 20°C with complete penetrance.
source: Even more surprising was the observation that dauer formation was also observed at 15°C and 20°C with complete penetrance (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations shown in Figures 2G and H.

claim: Dauer formation was related to the developmental speed at a given temperature: At 15°C, it took 6 days; at 20°C, it took 4 days; and at 25°C, it took 3 days to form dauers.
source: We found that dauer formation was related to the developmental speed at a given temperature: At 15°C, it took 6 days; at 20°C, it took 4 days; and at 25°C, it took 3 days to form dauers (Figure 2H).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations shown in Figure 2H.

claim: All auxin-induced DAF-2::degron dauers showed dauer-specific characteristics, such as SDS resistance, cessation of feeding, constricted pharynxes, and dauer-specific alae.
source: We verified that all auxin-induced DAF-2::degron dauers showed dauer-specific characteristics, such as SDS resistance, cessation of feeding, constricted pharynxes, and dauer-specific alae (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting a complete dauer transformation.
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental verification of dauer characteristics shown in figures.

claim: The AID of DAF-2 promotes complete dauer formation independent of temperature but dependent on DAF-2 protein abundance.
source: Thus, the AID of DAF-2 promotes complete dauer formation independent of temperature but dependent on DAF-2 protein abundance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temperature and dose-response experiments.

claim: When DAF-2 levels are below a given threshold at the mid-L1 stage, the animals commit to becoming dauers.
source: We found that when DAF-2 levels are below a given threshold at the mid-L1 stage, the animals commit to becoming dauers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temporal degradation experiments.

claim: daf-16 was required for dauer formation and developmental speed alterations after DAF-2::degron depletion.
source: We crossed DAF-2::degron with DAF-16::degron (Aghayeva et al., 2021) and found that daf-16 was required for dauer formation and developmental speed alterations after DAF-2::degron depletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental results from genetic crosses, with citation to the DAF-16::degron strain.

claim: No embryonic lethality nor L1 arrest was observed in the progeny of animals placed on 1 mM auxin as L4s.
source: We observed no embryonic lethality nor L1 arrest in the progeny of animals placed on 1 mM auxin as L4s.
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations.

claim: The inactivation of DAF-2 by AID is 100% penetrant for dauer formation at any temperature.
source: Taken together, the inactivation of DAF-2 by AID is 100% penetrant for dauer formation at any temperature.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the dauer formation experiments.

claim: The absence of embryonic lethality or L1 arrest at 1 mM auxin suggests that DAF-2::degron functionally is more similar to a non-conditional and severe loss-of-function mutation than a null allele.
source: Still, the absence of embryonic lethality or L1 arrest at 1 mM auxin suggests that DAF-2::degron functionally is more similar to a non-conditional and severe loss-of-function mutation than a null allele.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the phenotypic data comparing to known alleles.

claim: Auxin supplementation of DAF-2::degron animals, starting from L4, resulted in a 70–135% lifespan extension.
source: We found that auxin supplementation of DAF-2::degron animals, starting from L4, resulted in a 70–135% lifespan extension (Figure 3A; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative lifespan data shown in Figure 3A and supplementary file.

claim: DAF-2 degradation using 1 mM auxin surpassed the longevity of commonly used daf-2(e1368) and daf-2(e1370) mutants.
source: Impressively, DAF-2 degradation using 1 mM auxin surpassed the longevity of commonly used daf-2(e1368) and daf-2(e1370) mutants (Figure 3A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports comparative lifespan data shown in Figure 3A and supplementary file.

claim: Auxin treatment at 0.1 or 1 mM concentration had little or no effect on wild-type lifespan.
source: By contrast, auxin treatment at 0.1 or 1 mM concentration had little or no effect on wild-type lifespan (Figure 3A; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports control lifespan data shown in Figure 3A and supplementary file.

claim: Auxin-induced degradation of daf-2 is a powerful tool to promote longevity.
source: These results suggest that auxin-induced degradation of daf-2 is a powerful tool to promote longevity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lifespan extension data.

claim: Placing L4 DAF-2::degron animals on auxin and at 25°C resulted in similar levels of egg retention and effects on gonad size as was seen in the daf-2(e1370) class II allele.
source: In placing L4 DAF-2::degron animals on auxin and at 25°C, we observed similar levels of egg retention and effects on gonad size as was seen in the daf-2(e1370) class II allele.
evidence: The manuscript reports comparative phenotypic observations.

claim: Egg retention and germline shrinkage are temperature-sensitive traits, as DAF-2::degron animals did not retain eggs or had reduced gonad sizes at 15°C.
source: Strikingly, these effects were temperature-dependent, as DAF-2::degron animals did not retain eggs or had reduced gonad sizes at 15°C (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports temperature-dependent phenotypic data shown in figures.

claim: DAF-2::degron animals on auxin exhibited germline shrinkage at 25°C, albeit to a lesser degree than the daf-2(e1370) class II allele.
source: Similarly, DAF-2::degron animals on auxin exhibited germline shrinkage at 25°C, albeit to a lesser degree than the daf-2(e1370) class II allele (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports comparative phenotypic data shown in figures.

claim: No immobility of auxin-treated DAF-2::degron animals was observed at 25°C or during lifespan assays at 20°C.
source: We did not observe any immobility of auxin-treated DAF-2::degron animals at 25°C or during lifespan assays at 20°C (Video 1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The manuscript reports observational data with video evidence.

claim: Auxin-induced degradation of DAF-2 starting from L4 shortened body size of 2-day-old adults at both 15°C and 25°C.
source: Although the effects on body size of daf-2(e1370) class II allele are temperature-dependent, presenting at 25°C but not at 15°C (Ewald et al., 2015; Gems et al., 1998; McCulloch and Gems, 2003; Figure 3—figure supplement 1), auxin-induced degradation of DAF-2 starting from L4 shortened body size of 2-day-old adults at both temperatures (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports phenotypic data with citations to previous work, shown in figures.

claim: AID of DAF-2::degron starting from L4 reduced brood size at both 15°C and 25°C.
source: Similarly, while daf-2(e1370) mutants only exhibit reduced brood sizes at higher temperatures (Ewald et al., 2018; Gems et al., 1998), AID of DAF-2::degron starting from L4 reduced brood size at both 15°C and 25°C (Figure 3E).
evidence: The manuscript reports phenotypic data with citations to previous work, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Smaller body and brood size manifest as non-conditional traits, in keeping with insulin/IGF-1's role as an essential gene for these functions.
source: This suggests that smaller body and brood size manifest as non-conditional traits, in keeping with insulin/IGF-1's role as an essential gene for these functions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the phenotypic data in the context of known gene function.

claim: Some daf-2 class II mutant phenotypes, or pathologies, can be induced during adulthood independent of temperature and passing through the L2d stage is not required for the daf-2 class II mutant phenotypes to emerge in adult animals.
source: In summary, these results suggest that some daf-2 class II mutant phenotypes, or pathologies, can be induced during adulthood independent of temperature and that passing through the L2d stage is not required for the daf-2 class II mutant phenotypes to emerge in adult animals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temperature-independent phenotype data.

claim: Depletion of DAF-2 in neurons caused egg retention and germline shrinkage.
source: Nonetheless, we found that depletion of DAF-2 in neurons caused egg retention and germline shrinkage (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: The manuscript reports tissue-specific phenotypic data shown in Figures 3F and G.

claim: The germline shrinkage and egg retention phenotypes were temperature-dependent, suggesting some interaction of temperature and neuronal DAF-2 abundance.
source: Interestingly, the germline shrinkage and egg retention phenotypes were temperature-dependent, suggesting some interaction of temperature and neuronal DAF-2 abundance.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the temperature-dependent tissue-specific phenotype data.

claim: Some daf-2-phenotypes appear to emerge from a single tissue, whereas others might be due to an interplay between several tissues.
source: Thus, some daf-2-phenotypes appear to emerge from a single tissue, whereas others might be due to an interplay between several tissues.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tissue-specific phenotype data.

claim: Either neuronal or intestinal depletion of DAF-2 was alone sufficient to extend lifespan, although not to the extent as when DAF-2 is degraded in all tissues.
source: We found that either neuronal or intestinal depletion of DAF-2 was alone sufficient to extend lifespan, although not to the extent as when DAF-2 is degraded in all tissues (Figure 4A; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports tissue-specific lifespan data shown in Figure 4A and supplementary file.

claim: Auxin-induced degradation of DAF-2 in all tissues resulted in increased oxidative stress resistance, comparable to daf-2(e1370) mutants.
source: Auxin-induced degradation of DAF-2 in all tissues resulted in increased oxidative stress resistance, comparable to daf-2(e1370) mutants (Figure 4B).
evidence: The manuscript reports stress resistance data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Improved oxidative stress resistance was observed when DAF-2 was depleted in the intestine but not in neurons.
source: We observed improved oxidative stress resistance when we depleted DAF-2 in the intestine but not in neurons (Figure 4C and D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript reports tissue-specific stress resistance data shown in figures.

claim: Reducing DAF-2 levels, specifically in the intestine, promotes longevity and stress resistance without causing dauer-like phenotypes.
source: This implies that reducing DAF-2 levels, specifically in the intestine, promotes longevity and stress resistance without causing dauer-like phenotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tissue-specific phenotype and lifespan data.

claim: The lifespan extension in DAF-2::degron animals fully required skn-1 at 15°C.
source: We found that the lifespan extension in DAF-2::degron animals fully required skn-1 at 15°C.
evidence: The manuscript reports genetic interaction data from lifespan experiments.

claim: A loss of skn-1 extended the median lifespan of DAF-2::degron animals at 25°C.
source: Surprisingly, however, a loss of skn-1 extended the median lifespan of DAF-2::degron animals at 25°C (Figure 4E and F; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports genetic interaction data shown in Figures 4E and F and supplementary file.

claim: skn-1 may function independently from dauer-like reprogramming pathways at 15°C.
source: This suggests that skn-1 may function independently from dauer-like reprogramming pathways at 15°C.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the temperature-dependent genetic interaction data.

claim: The increased longevity seen in DAF-2::degron animals may result from a differential transcriptional program at higher temperatures compared to lower temperatures.
source: Furthermore, the increased longevity seen in DAF-2::degron animals may result from a differential transcriptional program at higher temperatures compared to lower temperatures.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the temperature-dependent genetic interaction data.

claim: Shifting animals past the reproductive period at day 10 and day 12 still led to an increase in lifespan by 48–72% and 49–57%, respectively.
source: We found that shifting the animals past the reproductive period at day 10 and day 12 still led to an increase in lifespan by 48–72% and 49–57%, respectively (Figure 5A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports late-life intervention lifespan data shown in Figure 5A and supplementary file.

claim: Lifespan extension of animals was observed by supplementing auxin very late during lifespan at day 21 or 25 of adulthood, at a time at which already approximately 50–75% of the population had died.
source: We observed lifespan extension of animals by supplementing auxin very late during lifespan at day 21 or 25 of adulthood, at a time at which already approximately 50–75% of the population had died (Figure 5B–D, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports very late-life intervention lifespan data shown in Figures 5B-D and supplementary file.

claim: AID of DAF-2 doubled the lifespan of animals when applied at day 21 or day 25 of adulthood.
source: Remarkably, AID of DAF-2 doubled the lifespan of these animals at this late stage (Figure 5A–D, Supplementary file 1). For example, when about three-quarters of the population had ceased by day 21 (Figure 5B) or day 25 (Figure 5D), and control-treated DAF-2::degron animals lived for just another 4 or 7 days, the auxin-treated DAF-2::degron animals lived for another 26 or 43 days, respectively (Figure 5B and D, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative very late-life intervention lifespan data shown in figures and supplementary file.

claim: Reducing insulin/IGF-1 receptor signaling is feasible in geriatric C. elegans.
source: This demonstrates that reducing insulin/IGF-1 receptor signaling is feasible in geriatric C. elegans.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the very late-life intervention data.

claim: Targeting the daf-2 signaling pathway late in life may be an effective strategy to extend lifespan.
source: Thus, our approach to selectively reduce DAF-2 protein in old animals suggests that targeting the daf-2 signaling pathway late in life may be an effective strategy to extend lifespan.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the late-life intervention data.

claim: Interventions at almost the end of life can increase lifespan.
source: In summary, we have demonstrated that interventions at almost the end of life can increase lifespan.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the very late-life intervention experiments.

claim: Auxin-induced degradation is suitable for targeting transmembrane receptors for non-invasive manipulations during developmental and longevity in vivo studies.
source: We have established that auxin-induced degradation is suitable for targeting transmembrane receptors for non-invasive manipulations during developmental and longevity in vivo studies.
evidence: This is a methodological conclusion drawn from the successful application of AID to DAF-2.

claim: Dauer-like traits are not a spill-over of reprogrammed physiology from developing L2d pre-dauers.
source: We reconciled a longstanding question by providing evidence that dauer-like traits are not a spill-over of reprogrammed physiology from developing L2d pre-dauers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that dauer-like traits can be induced in adults without passing through L2d.

claim: The essential growth-related functions of DAF-2 are causing deficits when applied during development or growth phases.
source: Instead, the essential growth-related functions of DAF-2 are causing deficits when applied during development or growth phases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phenotypic data showing growth defects with early DAF-2 depletion.

claim: Tissue-specific interventions or global interventions beyond reproduction or growth extend lifespan without pathology or deficits.
source: We have shown that tissue-specific interventions or global interventions beyond reproduction or growth extend lifespan without pathology or deficits.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the tissue-specific and late-life intervention data.

claim: DAF-2/insulin/IGF-1 receptor abundance is read-out to adapt metabolism to food abundance.
source: Degradation of DAF-2/insulin/IGF-1 receptor might not be an artificial intervention since DAF-2/insulin/IGF-1 receptor abundance is read-out to adapt metabolism to food abundance.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the food availability data showing DAF-2 level changes.

claim: Reducing insulin/insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-1 signaling (IIS) increases lifespan across species.
source: Reducing insulin/insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-1 signaling (IIS) increases lifespan across species, but the effects of reduced IIS interventions in extreme geriatric ages remains unknown.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: The effects of reduced IIS interventions in extreme geriatric ages remains unknown.
source: Reducing insulin/insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-1 signaling (IIS) increases lifespan across species, but the effects of reduced IIS interventions in extreme geriatric ages remains unknown.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: AID-mediated depletion of DAF-2 protein surpasses the longevity of daf-2 mutants.
source: Using this system, we found that AID-mediated depletion of DAF-2 protein surpasses the longevity of daf-2 mutants.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the lifespan experiments stated in the abstract.

claim: Depletion of DAF-2 during early adulthood resulted in multiple adverse phenotypes, including growth retardation, germline shrinkage, egg retention, and reduced brood size.
source: Depletion of DAF-2 during early adulthood resulted in multiple adverse phenotypes, including growth retardation, germline shrinkage, egg retention, and reduced brood size.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the phenotypic experiments stated in the abstract.

claim: AID-mediated depletion of DAF-2 post-reproduction, or specifically in the intestine in early adulthood, resulted in an extension of lifespan without deleterious effects.
source: By contrast, AID-mediated depletion of DAF-2 post-reproduction, or specifically in the intestine in early adulthood, resulted in an extension of lifespan without these deleterious effects.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the late-life and tissue-specific intervention experiments stated in the abstract.

claim: At geriatric ages, when 75% of the population had died, AID-mediated depletion of DAF-2 protein resulted in a doubling in lifespan.
source: Strikingly, at geriatric ages, when 75% of the population had died, AID-mediated depletion of DAF-2 protein resulted in a doubling in lifespan.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the very late-life intervention experiments stated in the abstract.

claim: Even close to the end of an individual's lifespan, it is possible to slow aging and promote longevity.
source: Thus, we provide a proof-of-concept that even close to the end of an individual's lifespan, it is possible to slow aging and promote longevity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: Mice heterozygous for the IGF-1 receptor are stress-resistant and long-lived.
source: Mice heterozygous for the IGF-1 receptor, or with depleted insulin receptor in adipose tissue, are stress-resistant and long-lived (Blüher et al., 2003; Holzenberger et al., 2003), for example, and several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the IIS pathway have been associated with human longevity (Kenyon, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citations.

claim: Mice with depleted insulin receptor in adipose tissue are stress-resistant and long-lived.
source: Mice heterozygous for the IGF-1 receptor, or with depleted insulin receptor in adipose tissue, are stress-resistant and long-lived (Blüher et al., 2003; Holzenberger et al., 2003), for example, and several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the IIS pathway have been associated with human longevity (Kenyon, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citations.

claim: Several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the IIS pathway have been associated with human longevity.
source: Mice heterozygous for the IGF-1 receptor, or with depleted insulin receptor in adipose tissue, are stress-resistant and long-lived (Blüher et al., 2003; Holzenberger et al., 2003), for example, and several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the IIS pathway have been associated with human longevity (Kenyon, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citation.

claim: Gene variants in the IGF-1 receptor have been associated and functionally linked with long lifespans in human centenarians.
source: Moreover, gene variants in the IGF-1 receptor have been associated and functionally linked with long lifespans in human centenarians (Suh et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citation.

claim: A single mutation in daf-2 could double the lifespan of C. elegans.
source: The groundbreaking discovery that a single mutation in daf-2, which is the orthologue of both the insulin and IGF-1 receptors (Kimura et al., 1997), or mutations in 'downstream' genes in the IIS pathway, could double the lifespan of an organism was made in the nematode C. elegans (Friedman and Johnson, 1988; Kenyon et al., 1993).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citations.

claim: daf-2 is the orthologue of both the insulin and IGF-1 receptors.
source: The groundbreaking discovery that a single mutation in daf-2, which is the orthologue of both the insulin and IGF-1 receptors (Kimura et al., 1997), or mutations in 'downstream' genes in the IIS pathway, could double the lifespan of an organism was made in the nematode C. elegans (Friedman and Johnson, 1988; Kenyon et al., 1993).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citation.

claim: Over 1000 papers on daf-2 have been published, making it one of the most studied genes in C. elegans.
source: Since its discovery, over 1000 papers on daf-2 have been published, making it one of the most studied genes in this model organism (Source: PubMed).
evidence: This is a statement about the literature with a source reference.

claim: The DAF-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor signaling regulates growth, development, metabolism, inter-tissue signaling, immunity, stress defense, and protein homeostasis, including extracellular matrix remodeling.
source: Genetic and genomics approaches have revealed that the DAF-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor signaling regulates growth, development, metabolism, inter-tissue signaling, immunity, stress defense, and protein homeostasis, including extracellular matrix remodeling (Ewald et al., 2015; Gems et al., 1998; Kimura et al., 1997; Murphy and Hu, 2013; Wolkow et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: Most daf-2 mutants develop into adults at 15°C and 20°C but enter the dauer stage at 25°C.
source: For instance, most daf-2 mutants develop into adults at 15°C and 20°C but enter the dauer stage at 25°C (Gems et al., 1998), which is a facultative and alternative larval endurance stage in which C. elegans spends most of its life cycle in the wild (Hu, 2007).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citations.

claim: The dauer stage is a facultative and alternative larval endurance stage in which C. elegans spends most of its life cycle in the wild.
source: For instance, most daf-2 mutants develop into adults at 15°C and 20°C but enter the dauer stage at 25°C (Gems et al., 1998), which is a facultative and alternative larval endurance stage in which C. elegans spends most of its life cycle in the wild (Hu, 2007).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citation.

claim: Several daf-2 alleles show L1 larval and pre-dauer stage (L2d) arrest.
source: A major limitation in using daf-2 mutants is that several of them show L1 larval and pre-dauer stage (L2d) arrest (Gems et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citation.

claim: The daf-2 alleles have been categorized into two mutant classes depending on the penetrance of dauer-like phenotypes during adulthood.
source: Furthermore, the daf-2 alleles have been categorized into two mutant classes depending on the penetrance of dauer-like phenotypes during adulthood, such as reduced brood size, small body size, and germline shrinkage, as observed in the daf-2 class II mutants (Arantes-Oliveira et al., 2003; Ewald et al., 2018; Ewald et al., 2015; Gems et al., 1998; Hess et al., 2019; Patel et al., 2008; Podshivalova and Kerr, 2017).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: RNA interference of daf-2 increases lifespan without dauer formation during development and circumvents induction of daf-2 class II mutant phenotypes during adulthood.
source: RNA interference of daf-2 can be applied, which increases lifespan without dauer formation during development and circumvents induction of daf-2 class II mutant phenotypes during adulthood (Dillin et al., 2002; Ewald et al., 2018; Ewald et al., 2015; Kennedy et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: The increase in lifespan by RNAi of daf-2 is only partial compared to strong alleles such as daf-2(e1370).
source: However, the increase in lifespan by RNAi of daf-2 is only partial compared to strong alleles such as daf-2(e1370) (Ewald et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citation.

claim: Adult-specific RNAi knockdown of daf-2 quickly loses its potential to increase lifespan and does not extend lifespan when started after day 6 of adulthood.
source: Furthermore, adult-specific RNAi knockdown of daf-2 quickly loses its potential to increase lifespan and does not extend lifespan when started after day 6 of adulthood (Dillin et al., 2002), that is, after the reproductive period of C. elegans.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citation.

claim: The Arabidopsis thaliana IAA17 degron is a 68-amino acid motif that is specifically recognized by the transport inhibitor response 1 (TIR1) protein only in the presence of the plant hormone auxin.
source: The Arabidopsis thaliana IAA17 degron is a 68-amino acid motif that is specifically recognized by the transport inhibitor response 1 (TIR1) protein only in the presence of the plant hormone auxin (indole-3-acetic acid; Dharmasiri et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citation.

claim: Cytoplasmic, nuclear, and membrane-binding proteins tagged with degron have been shown to be targeted and degraded in C. elegans.
source: Although cytoplasmic, nuclear, and membrane-binding proteins tagged with degron have been recently shown to be targeted and degraded in C. elegans (Beer et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2015), to our knowledge, the AID system has not been used previously to degrade transmembrane proteins, such as the DAF-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citations.

claim: To the authors' knowledge, the AID system has not been used previously to degrade transmembrane proteins, such as the DAF-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor.
source: Although cytoplasmic, nuclear, and membrane-binding proteins tagged with degron have been recently shown to be targeted and degraded in C. elegans (Beer et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2015), to our knowledge, the AID system has not been used previously to degrade transmembrane proteins, such as the DAF-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor.
evidence: This identifies a novelty of the current study.

claim: Using AID effectively degrades DAF-2 protein and promotes dauer formation when applied early in development.
source: We find that using AID effectively degrades DAF-2 protein and promotes dauer formation when applied early in development.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the developmental experiments.

claim: Dauer-like phenotypes are present in adults when AID of DAF-2 is applied late in development.
source: Dauer-like phenotypes are present in adults when AID of DAF-2 is applied late in development.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the developmental timing experiments.

claim: Some adulthood dauer traits are induced by the loss of daf-2 in neurons, but others seem to be caused by the systemic loss of daf-2.
source: Some of these adulthood dauer traits are induced by the loss of daf-2 in neurons, but others seem to be caused by the systemic loss of daf-2.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the tissue-specific experiments.

claim: The post-developmental, conditional degradation of DAF-2 protein extends lifespan without introducing dauer-like phenotypes.
source: More importantly, the post-developmental, conditional degradation of DAF-2 protein extends lifespan without introducing dauer-like phenotypes.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the post-developmental intervention experiments.

claim: When more than half of the population has died at day 25 of adulthood, AID of DAF-2 in these remaining aged animals is sufficient to promote longevity.
source: Remarkably, we demonstrate that when more than half of the population has died at day 25 of adulthood, AID of DAF-2 in these remaining aged animals is sufficient to promote longevity.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the very late-life intervention experiments.

claim: Therapeutics applied at even extremely late stages of life are capable of increasing longevity and healthspan in animals.
source: Our work suggests that therapeutics applied at even extremely late stages of life are capable of increasing longevity and healthspan in animals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the very late-life intervention data.

claim: Mutant DAF-2(e1370) protein is present at 15°C but barely detected at 25°C.
source: Previously, Kimura and colleagues used DAF-2 antibody immunostaining of whole animals and reported that mutant DAF-2(e1370) protein is present at 15°C but barely detected at 25°C, whereas mutant DAF-2(e1370) protein in a daf-16 null background or wild-type DAF-2 protein persists at both 15°C and 25°C (Kimura et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: Upon 24 hr of starvation, the DAF-2 receptor is no longer detectable by using immunofluorescence in fixed C. elegans.
source: By contrast, upon 24 hr of starvation, the DAF-2 receptor is no longer detectable by using immunofluorescence in fixed C. elegans (Kimura et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: DAF-2 protein levels may be autoregulated by IIS and might be influenced by temperature and food availability.
source: Since the FOXO transcription factor daf-16 is the transcriptional output of daf-2 signaling (Ewald et al., 2018; Gems et al., 1998), these results suggest that DAF-2 protein levels may be autoregulated by IIS and might be influenced by temperature and food availability.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on previous findings with citations.

claim: Activation of DAF-2/insulin/IGF-1 receptor induces a downstream kinase cascade to phosphorylate the transcription factors DAF-16/FOXO and SKN-1/NRF, causing their retention in the cytoplasm.
source: Activation of DAF-2/insulin/IGF-1 receptor induces a downstream kinase cascade to phosphorylate the transcription factors DAF-16/FOXO and SKN-1/NRF, causing their retention in the cytoplasm (Figure 2A; Ewald et al., 2015; Henderson and Johnson, 2001; Lin et al., 2001; Murphy et al., 2003; Ogg et al., 1997; Tullet et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with multiple citations and reference to a figure.

claim: Genetic inhibition of daf-2 results in less DAF-16 and SKN-1 phosphorylation and promotes nuclear translocation to induce the expression of target genes, such as sod-3 and gst-4.
source: Genetic inhibition of daf-2 results in less DAF-16 and SKN-1 phosphorylation and promotes nuclear translocation to induce the expression of target genes, such as sod-3 (superoxide dismutase) and gst-4 (glutathione S-transferase), respectively (Ewald et al., 2015; Henderson and Johnson, 2001; Lin et al., 2001; Murphy et al., 2003; Tullet et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: Mosaic loss of daf-2 in different cell lineages indicated neurons as crucial tissue to control dauer formation non-cell autonomously.

evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: Dauer formation in daf-2(e1370) can be restored by expressing wild-type DAF-2 only in neurons.

evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: Transgenic expression of wild-type copies of DAF-2 in neuronal or intestinal cells was shown to partially suppress the longevity of daf-2(e1370) mutants at 25°C.

evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: skn-1 activity is necessary for full lifespan extension of daf-2(e1370) mutants only at 15°C but not at 25°C.
source: Intriguingly, skn-1 activity is necessary for full lifespan extension of daf-2(e1370) mutants only at 15°C but not at 25°C (Ewald et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: Mid-life administration of IGF-1 receptor monoclonal antibodies to 78-week-old mice is sufficient to increase their lifespan and improve their healthspan.
source: In mammals, mid-life administration of IGF-1 receptor monoclonal antibodies to 78-week-old mice (a time when all mice are still alive and 6 weeks before first mice start to die) is sufficient to increase their lifespan and improve their healthspan (Mao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: Mice carrying brain-specific heterozygous IGF-1 receptor knockout are long-lived.
source: Mice carrying brain-specific heterozygous IGF-1 receptor knockout are long-lived (Kappeler et al., 2008), as are the mice with adipose-specific knockout of the insulin receptor (Blüher et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: Mice with adipose-specific knockout of the insulin receptor are long-lived.
source: Mice carrying brain-specific heterozygous IGF-1 receptor knockout are long-lived (Kappeler et al., 2008), as are the mice with adipose-specific knockout of the insulin receptor (Blüher et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: Starving rats for 3 days increases the abundance of insulin-bound insulin receptors.
source: Starving rats for 3 days increases the abundance of insulin-bound insulin receptors (Koopmans et al., 1995), possibly to increase glucose uptake.
evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation and interpretation.

claim: Heterozygous IGF-1 receptor knockout mice, which have lower IGF-1 receptor levels, have an increased lifespan.
source: However, alterations of the IGF-1 receptor levels are associated with altered lifespan. For instance, heterozygous IGF-1 receptor knockout mice, which have lower IGF-1 receptor levels, have an increased lifespan (Holzenberger et al., 2003; Kappeler et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2014).

claim: Overexpression of the short isoform of p53 (p44) increases IGF-1 receptor levels and shortens the lifespan of mice.

claim: The administration of recombinant human IGF-1 increases IGF-1 receptor abundance in murine embryonic cells.

evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: Palmitate activates PPARα to induce miR-15b, which targets insulin receptor mRNA for degradation.
source: For instance, palmitate activates PPARα to induce miR-15b, which targets insulin receptor mRNA for degradation (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: The E3 ligase CHIP regulates insulin/IGF-1 receptor levels in C. elegans, Drosophila, and human cell cultures.

evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

evidence: This is a statement of previous findings with citation.

source: Taken together, these observations suggest that food abundance controls mammalian insulin receptor levels via E3 ligase-mediated degradation.

claim: Nutritional cues may regulate insulin/IGF-1 receptor levels via a variety of mechanisms, including ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, across species.
source: Although in C. elegans we found the opposite changes in DAF-2 receptor levels, that is, they were reduced upon starvation and increased upon high glucose feeding, our observations suggest that nutritional cues may regulate insulin/IGF-1 receptor levels via a variety of mechanisms, including ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, across species.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the current study's data and previous literature.
